intent: Let a user pick exactly one option from a small visible set, tracked as one shared value.
typical_uses: A short list of mutually exclusive options where every choice stays visible at once (plan tier, delivery method, sort order)

dont_use_when.situation: More options than fit comfortably on screen at once, or the space is constrained
Independent options where more than one may be on at once
A single on/off setting with no sibling options

invariants.text: `value` and `defaultValue` are both accepted; `defaultValue` seeds the initial state and is ignored afterwards, and when `value` is given it wins and the component follows it on every render.
Setting `disabled` on the group disables every item inside it; an item's own `disabled` can disable that one item further but cannot re-enable it against a disabled group.

anti_patterns.dont: Render the group with no accessible name
anti_patterns.do_instead: Pass `aria-label`, or `aria-labelledby` pointing at a visible heading (or at a FieldLegend inside a FieldSet); a `<label htmlFor>` cannot name the group, because the group is not a labelable element

a11y.by: Base UI's own RadioGroup primitive (role="radiogroup", arrow-key navigation between items, a hidden native input for form submission) plus radio-group.test.tsx's own role/aria-checked/data-checked assertions

value.states: value is the root's own generic Value type parameter, not a JSON Schema type
value.because: Base UI's `RadioGroup<Value>` types `value` as `Value | undefined`, where `Value` is the caller's own choice - no JSON Schema type can state it, only that something is accepted. radio-group.md's example uses string item values (`value="free"` on the item), so a group value is typically one of those strings.

defaultValue.states: defaultValue is the root's own generic Value type parameter, not a JSON Schema type
defaultValue.because: Same generic type as `value` above, unchecked in the same half - the uncontrolled starting selection is one of the caller's own `Value` type, which no schema can state because the caller chooses it.

onValueChange.states: onValueChange is a callback, not a value
onValueChange.because: `(value: Value, eventDetails) => void` - a function of the root's own generic `Value` plus Base UI's own event-details object. No JSON Schema type covers a function.

inputRef.states: inputRef is a ref to the hidden native input Base UI renders for form submission
inputRef.because: `React.Ref<HTMLInputElement>` is a union of a ref object and a callback function - the compiler emits one JSON type per property. It exists so a consumer can read or focus the native input directly, the same input `name`/`form` submit through.

render.states: render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies
render.because: Base UI's render prop takes an element or a function of the group's own state, so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - the compiler emits one JSON type per property.

style.states: style accepts a function of the group's state as well as a plain style object
style.because: Base UI widens React's `CSSProperties` to `CSSProperties | ((state) => CSSProperties)` so a caller can style off the primitive's own state (disabled, readOnly, required, ...). The compiler emits one JSON type per property, so nothing is asserted; the kit's own styling goes through radio-group.module.css, not through this.

good.title: Controlled group, each item captioned by a sibling Label
good.code:
<RadioGroup value={tier} onValueChange={setTier} aria-label="Plan tier">
  <RadioGroupItem value="free" id="tier-free" />
  <Label htmlFor="tier-free">Free</Label>
  <RadioGroupItem value="pro" id="tier-pro" />
  <Label htmlFor="tier-pro">Pro</Label>
  <RadioGroupItem value="enterprise" id="tier-enterprise" disabled />
  <Label htmlFor="tier-enterprise">Enterprise (contact us)</Label>
</RadioGroup>

good.title: Uncontrolled group with a default selection
good.code:
<RadioGroup defaultValue="pro" name="tier" aria-label="Plan tier">
  <RadioGroupItem value="free" aria-label="Free" />
  <RadioGroupItem value="pro" aria-label="Pro" />
</RadioGroup>

bad.title: A single yes/no option modeled as a one-item group
bad.code:
<RadioGroup value={agreed ? 'yes' : 'no'} onValueChange={(v) => setAgreed(v === 'yes')}>
  <RadioGroupItem value="yes" /> I agree
</RadioGroup>
bad.why: One option is not a choice - the group's arrow-key navigation and single-selection machinery have nothing to coordinate. Reach for `Checkbox` instead.
